content: 1. The metabolism of panobinostat via the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 is affected by co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. In such cases, the starting dose of panobinostat should be reduced to 10 mg. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 2. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Both clarithromycin and paroxetine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 7. Both clarithromycin and pasireotide prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 8. Both clarithromycin and pazopanib prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of perampanel by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pimozide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 17. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially increasing polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. 19. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Both clarithromycin and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels of pravastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for myopathy, and do not exceed a pravastatin dose of 40 mg/day when co-administered with clarithromycin. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 22. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. There is a risk of toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of propafenone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quazepam by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Both clarithromycin and quetiapine increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quinine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Both clarithromycin and ranolazine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 33. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Rifampin also decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of riociguat by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels of rilpivirine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 38. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 40. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both clarithromycin and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels of rosiglitazone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. This may result in hypoglycemia; monitor glucose levels closely. 45. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 46. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Valsartan is a substrate of the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1, and co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. 47. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and salmeterol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored.
